newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco says strike trims Q2 earnings.
newsitem.headline: Inco says strike trims Q2 earnings.

text.p: Canadian nickel giant Inco Ltd said on Monday a strike at its Sudbury, Ontario operations trimmed US$20 million from its second-quarter earnings.
Inco reported net income of US$16 million or US$0.05 a share for the second quarter, versus year earlier net income of US$61 million or US$0.47 a share.
A 26-day strike at Inco's Ontario division, which ended on June 28, resulted in an after-tax cost of US$20 million or US$0.12 a share in the second quarter.

"Strike expenses are those ongoing costs...incurred during the strike period which would normally be treated as production costs and charged to inventory, but in the absence of production, have been expensed," Inco said in a statement.
The new three-year labor agreement would have a minimal impact on the division's production costs due to efficiency improvements in the contract, Inco said.
Inco said the drop in second-quarter earnings was also due to lower prices for nickel, cobalt and copper, and costs associated with the rebuild of furnace no. 1 at P.T. Inco.
